comparator.name: Dutch Languages and Cultures — Dutch Language and Culture route
comparator.sourceNotes: The current generic bachelor is Dutch Languages and Cultures (ISAT 50479). Its 2026–27 programme-specific Teaching and Examination Regulations define two formal tracks, Dutch Language and Culture and Frisian Language and Culture. Neither language-specific track is inherently broader or less specialized than the other, so the Dutch Language and Culture track is selected by the neutral official-order tie-break; it is listed first in the regulation. This choice is made before and independently of UCR fit. For students beginning in September 2026, the selected track has a coherent 60+60+60=180 EC curriculum. The second- and third-year parts take effect in 2027–28 and 2028–29 as this cohort progresses. The 30-EC minor remains genuine open curricular space and is not populated with an invented subject.
components: Open minor space; no optional minor subject is universally compulsory.

routeSelection.basis: The generic target covers a current bachelor with two equally formal, language-specific tracks: Dutch Language and Culture and Frisian Language and Culture. Current official evidence does not establish either as more representative, broader or less specialized. The Dutch Language and Culture track is therefore selected because it is listed first in the current official regulation, applying the neutral official-order tie-break before any UCR fit assessment.

exception.reason: The selected route is a discipline-specific Dutch Studies degree whose compulsory spine combines Dutch phonology, syntax, semantics and language acquisition with historical and present-day Dutch, medieval, early-modern and modern Dutch literature, advanced Dutch-language proficiency, research workshops and a Dutch Studies thesis. UCR offers one introductory Dutch course plus genuine general courses in literature, rhetoric, communication and psycholinguistics, but those courses do not provide a sustained advanced Dutch-language, Dutch-linguistics and Dutch-literature sequence. Constructing a 24-course UCR schedule from broader adjacent subjects would change the named academic field and leave the defining Dutch core uncovered.
exception.curriculumContext: The exact 2026–27 regulation accounts for all 180 EC in the selected Dutch Language and Culture route for the September 2026 cohort. Its second- and third-year curriculum is introduced in 2027–28 and 2028–29 as that cohort progresses. The exception is therefore based on the absence of defensible UCR curricular depth, not on uncertainty about the comparator's route or credit total.
exception.ucrCourseEvidence: Read all 151 current rows in data/reference/ucr_courses_enriched.xlsx, including descriptions, outline profiles, disciplines, topics, methods, prerequisites and planned terms. MCCCOMM112 Dutch teaches basic oral and written communication for everyday situations and cultural orientation; it is not an academic Dutch linguistics or literature sequence. MCCLITR111 Introduction to Literary Studies, MCCLITR112 Great Literary Works, MCCLITR211 World Myth & Literature, MCCLITR212 Life & Travel Writing, MCCLITR311 Film & Text and MCCLITR312 Perspectives on Literary Meaning provide broad literary study. MCCCOMM111 The Art of Rhetorical Communication, MCCCOMM211 Style & Meaning, MCCCOMM213 Rhetoric in Action, MCCCOMM311 Persuasive Communication and MCCCOMM312 Creative Communication Laboratory provide adjacent rhetoric and communication work. HCBGATE102 Introduction to Brain & Behavior, HCBCOGN311 Higher Order Functions and HCBCOGN312 Psycholinguistics provide adjacent cognitive-language content, while HCBPSYC211 Statistics & Experimental Methods, HCBPSYC313 Advanced Research Seminar and GOSHIST312 History Research Seminar provide general research support. Current prerequisite and term fields were checked for every cited course. None supplies the missing Dutch phonology and syntax progression, historical Dutch, advanced Dutch proficiency, the required sequence of Dutch literary periods, or a Dutch Studies research capstone. No defensible 24-course closest match can therefore be scheduled.
